statement: You are given an undirected graph: a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1), a list of edges, and a vertex start. Each vertex's neighbours are kept in the order their edges appear in the list.
Traverse the graph breadth-first from start: use a queue, mark a vertex visited when it is enqueued, and each time you dequeue a vertex, enqueue its unvisited neighbours in order.
Return the order in which vertices leave the queue. Vertices that cannot be reached from start do not appear.

examples.explanation: Level 1 is {1, 2}, level 2 is {3, 4}, and 5 is reached last, three edges from 0. It is enqueued once, by 3, even though 4 is also its neighbour.
On a simple path each level has exactly one vertex, so BFS walks the path in order.
